response:
It makes sense that you feel worn down. Hearing daily complaints—especially about a painful family situation you didn't create—can be exhausting, and it's okay to have limits on what you can absorb.

Setting a boundary doesn't mean you don't care. You might tell your mother something honest and kind, like, "I love you and I want to support you, but I can't do a long call every day. Can we talk twice a week, and could you also reach out to someone who can help share this load?" It may help to gently point her toward practical support, since raising a child alone is a lot for her too. You're allowed to protect your own energy while still loving your family. Choosing what you can realistically give isn't selfish—it's what makes it possible to keep showing up at all.
